newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila denies Vietnam rice bought at higher price.
newsitem.headline: Manila denies Vietnam rice bought at higher price.

text.p: The Philippine's National Food Authority (NFA) on Monday denied it bought "overpriced" rice from Vietnam.

NFA deputy administrator Gregorio Tan aired the denial in an interview with radio station DZRH on reports that Vietnam rice was being traded around $235 per tonne FOB against the $291.50 C&F clinched by the NFA.
"Even if it's true that you can buy rice at $235 per tonne FOB, you are not sure that you can bring out the rice because the Vietnamese rice market is a regulated market," Tan said.
Last month, the NFA signed a contract to buy 100,000 tonnes of rice from Vietnam Southern Foods Corp. The contract also carried an option for the supply of another 100,000 tonnes, Tan said.
Tan said the NFA negotiated with a state owned company of Vietnam for its rice imports to ensure immediate supply before July this year.
"In 1992 and 1995, some Philippine traders and local government units which contracted Vietnamese rice were unable to take deliveries of their orders," Tan said.
